title: Tor computed by an augmented flat resolution
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M and N be R-modules, and F a nonnegative chain complex of R-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Let epsilon:F -> M[0] be a quasi-isomorphism, so F is an augmented resolution of M. Suppose every term F_i is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For every natural degree j, there is an R-module isomorphism Tor^R_j(M,N) [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] = H_j(F tensor_R N). No boundedness or finite generation assumption is needed.

proof.text: Take a projective resolution Q of N and form the commuting first-quadrant tensor bicomplex F_p tensor Q_q. Its rows are exact in positive degrees since Q_q is projective and hence flat, and F resolves M. Its columns are exact in positive degrees by flatness of F_p and exactness of Q. The quasi-isomorphism of F at zero gives exactness of F_1 -> F_0 -> M and surjectivity onto M.

Use right exactness of tensor to identify the column cokernel complex with F tensor N and the row cokernel complex with Q tensor M (braiding in the latter identification). Define these maps by the augmentation on each component, descend through opcycles, and verify they are isomorphisms by degreewise exactness and surjectivity. The positive exactness hypotheses give the homology isomorphism between both cokernel complexes by the double-complex comparison.

The projective resolution Q computes Tor_prime(N,M) by Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.isoLeftDerivedObj. Apply Tor symmetry to identify Tor_prime(M,N) with this module and compose with the preceding homology isomorphisms. The proof works also in degree zero and for zero modules.

theorem flatResolution_torComparison
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (F : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℕ)
    (ε : F ⟶ (ChainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj M)
    [QuasiIso ε] (hflat : ∀ i : ℕ, Module.Flat R (F.X i))
    (N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (j : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) j).obj M).obj N) ≅
      (((tensorRight N).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)).obj F).homology j)
